title: Jump Game III
prompt: You are given an array of non-negative integers `arr` and a starting index `start`. When you are at index `i`, you can jump to `i + arr[i]` or `i - arr[i]`, as long as the resulting index is within the bounds of the array. Return `true` if you can reach any index in `arr` with value `0`, or `false` otherwise. You cannot jump outside of the array at any time.

examples.explanation: One valid path: index 5 -> index 4 -> index 1 -> index 3, which holds 0.
From index 2 you can only reach index 0 or index 4, and from there you can never reach the 0 at index 1.
The starting index itself already holds 0, so no jumps are needed at all.

hints: Model each index as a node in a graph where an edge exists from i to i + arr[i] and from i to i - arr[i] (when in bounds) — this is really graph reachability, not a true 2D grid, but the same BFS/DFS flood-fill idea applies.
Do a BFS or DFS starting from `start`, marking visited indices so you don't revisit them and loop forever.
You can stop as soon as you visit any index whose value is 0 — return true immediately; if the search exhausts all reachable indices without finding one, return false.

solution.approach: Treat each array index as a node with up to two outgoing edges (i + arr[i] and i - arr[i], when in bounds), and run BFS or DFS from `start`, tracking visited indices to avoid infinite loops from back-and-forth jumps. Since jumps can only produce a fixed set of reachable indices, this exploration terminates and correctly answers reachability to any index holding 0.
